newsitem.title: USA: Benign tumor removed from Liz Taylor's brain.
newsitem.headline: Benign tumor removed from Liz Taylor's brain.

text.p: Neurosurgeons operated on actress Elizabeth Taylor for four hours on Thursday to remove a benign brain tumour, a hospital spokesman said.
Ron Wise, of the Cedars-Sinai Medical Centre, said the surgery "went as planned" and Taylor was recovering.

The tumour, on the left side of Taylor's brain, was detected this month during a brain scan as part of a routine physical examination. Doctors expect Taylor, who will be 65 next week, to recover without complications.

Dr. Martin Cooper, Clinical Chief of Neurosurgery at the famed Beverly Hills hospital, who performed the operation, was to hold a news conference later to explain how the surgery went, Wise said. Taylor was in the operating theatre from around 8 a.m. PST (11 a.m. EST 1600 GMT) until about noon (3 p.m. EST ,2000 GMT) the spokesman said.
The operation, originally scheduled for Feb. 17, was postponed partly because Taylor had been suffering from the flu and also because of a scheduling conflict with her surgeons.
Taylor attended a gala 65th birthday party in Hollywood on Sunday to benefit AIDS research. Her actual birthday is Feb. 27.
